title: Vanish
content:
Sneha's curiosity had reached its peak.

Unable to hold herself back any longer, she looked at Siddu with eager eyes.

"So... what happened after that?" she asked.

Siddu remained silent for a moment. His expression grew distant, as if he were reliving memories he had tried hard to bury. After a deep breath, he finally spoke.

"We spent so many wonderful days together," he said softly. "Life was beautiful... until the end of our first year of Intermediate. Then, without any warning, she disappeared. She left without telling me anything. I kept calling her again and again, hoping she'd answer just once... but she never did."

His voice trembled ever so slightly.

"I was completely shattered. I tried every possible way to reach her. I contacted all of her friends, begged them to tell me where she was or what had happened... but every attempt failed. No one gave me an answer. It was as if she had vanished from my life."

Sneha listened in complete silence.

The pain hidden behind Siddu's calm voice touched her heart. She couldn't imagine how helpless he must have felt during those days.

Just then, the shrill ringtone of Siddu's phone broke the silence.

He glanced at the screen and stood up.

"I'll be back in a minute," he said before walking out of the compartment to answer the call.

Sneha nodded.

She patiently waited for him to return, her mind completely occupied by his unfinished story. Every passing minute only made her curiosity grow stronger.

Five minutes passed.

Then ten.

Sneha's eyes drifted toward the compartment entrance again and again.

But Siddu never returned.

As the train slowed down, it arrived at another station. Passengers stepped onto the platform while vendors rushed past the windows calling out for customers. Feeling a little hungry, Sneha walked to a nearby stall to buy something.

A few minutes later, she returned to her seat.

The moment she looked up, her heart skipped a beat.

Siddu's backpack...

His luggage...

Everything was gone.

She stood frozen, unable to process what she was seeing.

Without wasting another second, she hurried through the coach, checking every seat before searching the neighbouring compartments. She walked from one end of the train to the other, hoping to find him.

But Siddu had disappeared without leaving a trace.

Disappointed, she slowly returned to her seat.

As she sat down, something caught her attention.

A neatly folded piece of paper rested on the seat beside her.

Curious, she picked it up and unfolded it.

The note read—

"Sorry, Sneha.

Something important came up, so I had to get off the train midway without informing you.

You're one of the kindest people I've ever met. Please don't trust everyone so easily. This world isn't as kind as you are.

Take care."

Sneha silently folded the letter and held it in her hands.

For a brief moment, concern replaced her disappointment.

But the feeling quickly turned into irritation.

"Seriously?" she murmured to herself. "He didn't even leave his phone number."

She leaned back in her seat, thinking of every possible way she could find him.

Who was Siddu really?

Would she ever get to know the rest of his story?

The questions refused to leave her mind.

Just then, her phone vibrated.

For a split second, she hoped it might somehow be Siddu.

But the screen displayed another name.

Mom Calling...

Sneha answered the call.

"Hello, Mom..."

"Hi, Sneha. How's your journey going?" her mother asked warmly.

"It's going fine," Sneha replied, though the dullness in her voice was impossible to hide.

The two spoke for a few minutes about ordinary things before ending the call.

Even after hanging up, Siddu's unfinished story continued to occupy her thoughts.

Lost in those thoughts, she eventually drifted into a light sleep.

Hours passed.

When she finally opened her eyes, darkness had covered the sky outside the train.

The train came to a halt at another station.

Sneha stepped onto the platform, stretched her tired body, took a deep breath of the cool night air, and climbed back into the coach.

She quietly opened her dinner and began eating.

Halfway through the meal, an idea suddenly flashed across her mind.

She immediately grabbed her phone and called one of her close friends.

After the call connected, she quickly explained everything that had happened and requested a favor.

"I only know his seat number," she said. "Can you somehow find the passenger details?"

"Give me a few minutes," her friend replied before ending the call.

Sneha placed the phone beside her and waited impatiently.

Every passing minute felt longer than the last.

Finally, her phone rang again.

She answered instantly.

"Did you find anything?" she asked without wasting a second.

Her friend hesitated before replying.

"I found the reservation details... but there's something strange."

"What is it?"

"The ticket wasn't booked in Siddharth's name."

Sneha frowned.

"Then whose name was it?"

There was a brief silence before her friend answered.

"Kiran."

For a moment, Sneha was speechless.

"And the registered phone number is..." her friend began.

Just then—

Her phone suddenly went dead.

The battery had completely drained.

"Oh, come on!" Sneha exclaimed in frustration.

She hurriedly plugged the charger into the charging socket near her seat and waited impatiently.

Every second felt unbearable.

As soon as the phone switched on, she immediately called her friend again.

But this time...

No Network.

The call failed.

Sneha clenched her teeth in irritation.

"First the battery dies... and now there's no signal?"

She stared helplessly at the screen while the train sped through an area with almost no network coverage.

Several minutes later, a single network bar finally appeared.

Without wasting another second, she immediately redialed her friend's number.

This time...

She was determined to uncover the truth behind Siddu's mysterious disappearance.
